desc:
Every node of a singly linked list has, besides next, a random pointer that points to any node of the same list (possibly itself) or to nothing.

Encoding. The list has n nodes. vals[i] is the value of the i-th node (0-based, head first) and random[i] is the index of the node its random pointer points to, or -1 for null. Both arrays have the same length.

Build a deep copy of the list: n brand new nodes with the same values, whose next and random pointers only point to nodes of the copy, never to the original. Return the copy in the same form, one row per node from head to tail: [value, randomIndex], where randomIndex is the position of the copy's random target within the copy, or -1.

For example vals = [7,13,11] with random = [-1,0,2] (the first node points nowhere, the second points to the first, the third to itself) gives [[7,-1],[13,0],[11,2]].

The original list must stay unchanged. Try to do it in O(n) time with O(1) extra space apart from the copy itself, i.e. without a hash map.
hints: The next pointers are easy to copy in one pass. The problem is a random pointer of the copy that needs the copy of a node that may not exist yet.

A hash map from original node to copied node solves it in two passes: first create all copies, then wire next and random through the map. To avoid the map, you need a different way to find 'the copy of node x'.
Interleave: insert each copy directly after its original (A, A', B, B', ...). Then the copy of x.random is simply x.random.next. Finally pull the two lists apart again, restoring the original.
editorial: Map approach: pass 1 creates a copy of every node and stores copy[orig]; pass 2 sets copy[orig].next = copy[orig.next] and copy[orig].random = copy[orig.random]. That is O(n) time and O(n) extra space for the map.

O(1)-extra-space approach in three passes. (1) For each original node insert its copy right after it. (2) For each original node x with a random pointer set x.next.random = x.random.next: the node after any original is its copy, so this is exactly 'the copy of the random target'. (3) Walk the interleaved list and split it into the original list (restored) and the copy list. Finally read the copy list out; the index of a random target is its position in that list. Total O(n) time.
solution:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.val = val
        self.next = None
        self.random = None


def copyRandomList(vals, random):
    n = len(vals)
    if n == 0:
        return []
    nodes = [Node(v) for v in vals]
    for i in range(n):
        if i + 1 < n:
            nodes[i].next = nodes[i + 1]
        if random[i] >= 0:
            nodes[i].random = nodes[random[i]]
    head = nodes[0]
    # 1. weave a copy behind every node
    cur = head
    while cur:
        c = Node(cur.val)
        c.next = cur.next
        cur.next = c
        cur = c.next
    # 2. copy the random pointers
    cur = head
    while cur:
        if cur.random:
            cur.next.random = cur.random.next
        cur = cur.next.next
    # 3. split the two lists
    new_head = head.next
    cur = head
    while cur:
        c = cur.next
        cur.next = c.next
        c.next = c.next.next if c.next else None
        cur = cur.next
    # read the copy out
    index = {}
    order = []
    c = new_head
    while c:
        index[id(c)] = len(order)
        order.append(c)
        c = c.next
    return [[c.val, index[id(c.random)] if c.random else -1] for c in order]
